F.n: Shima Gourmet ROCO, Iriomote (島ぐるめ ROCO)
F.ad: 58 Uehara, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Uehara dining room cooking Iriomote's sea and mountain catch — grilled crab, sashimi salad, squid-ink rice croquettes and grouper simmered in island salt.

F.n: Umi-no-Eki Ayahashi-kan, Kaichū-dōro (海の駅 あやはし館)
F.w: The 'sea station' halfway along the 5 km Kaichū-dōro causeway: local produce and the Kaichū Chaya restaurant upstairs serving soki soba and taco rice over the shallows.

F.n: Nuchi Māsu Salt Factory, Miyagi Island (ぬちまーす観光製塩ファクトリー)
F.w: Clifftop salt works across the Kaichū-dōro on Miyagi Island, where a patented spray-drying method snows mineral-rich salt inside the factory; free 10-minute tours every 20 minutes, a sea-view restaurant and shop.

F.n: Awamori Masahiro Gallery, Itoman (泡盛まさひろギャラリー)
F.w: Gallery-shop of Masahiro Distillery (founded 1883): watch the production line through glass, browse displays on awamori's history and taste for free.

F.n: Uema Kashiten Factory — Suppaiman (上間菓子店 工場見学)
F.w: Free factory tour of the maker of Suppaiman, Okinawa's cult dried-plum snack and its mascot; watch the plums and candies being made (video only on Saturdays).

F.n: Restaurant Marumi-ya, Zamami (レストラン まるみ屋)
F.ad: Zamami village, Zamami Island, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Five minutes from Zamami port: hearty daily set lunches built on island produce — mozuku seaweed champuru and house-made jīmāmi peanut tofu are the favourites.

F.n: Karaoke Izakaya Marine Box, Tokashiki (カラオケ居酒屋マリンボックス)
F.w: The port-side all-rounder of Tokashiki village: an A-lunch plate at midday, then island izakaya dishes and karaoke until midnight.

F.n: Hanagasa Shokudō (花笠食堂)
F.w: A popular old-style shokudō off the Heiwa-dōri arcade serving Okinawan home cooking as set meals: pick white, brown or red (sekihan) rice and one of five soups including inamuruchi and nakami-jiru. Its sweet house iced tea is famous enough to have been sold in cartons.

F.n: Uchinā Chaya Buku-Buku, Tsuboya (うちなー茶屋 ぶくぶく)
F.w: A small teahouse on Tsuboya's pottery street that whips bukubuku-cha, the frothy rice-and-jasmine tea with Ryūkyū-dynasty roots, in front of you. Named in Visit Okinawa's Naha guide.

F.n: COFFEE potohoto, Sakaemachi (コーヒー ポトホト)
F.w: A tiny self-roasting coffee stand inside the post-war Sakaemachi Market, whose owner placed 5th at the 2014 Japan Coffee Roasting Championship per Rurubu. Mapple names it among Sakaemachi's recommended stops.

F.n: Yagi Ryōri Misaki, Sakaemachi (山羊料理 美咲)
F.w: A goat-meat specialist in the Sakaemachi Market alleys — goat is a traditional Okinawan celebration food. Featured by both Stars and Stripes' Sakaemachi guide and Mapple's Sakaemachi restaurant roundup.

F.n: Sangoza Kitchen (さんご座キッチン)
F.w: A café-bar inside Sakurazaka Gekijō, Naha's historic art-house cinema, five minutes from the Heiwa-dōri market arcade, with a selection of awamori, beer, wine and sake. Mapple lists it among the Kokusai-dōri area's cheap-drinking (senbero) stops.

F.n: Ryūkyū Kashidokoro Ryūgū, Heiwa-dōri (琉球菓子処 琉宮 平和通り店)
F.w: A sātā andāgī specialist on the Heiwa-dōri market arcade off Kokusai-dōri, frying its own flour blend in plain, brown-sugar, coconut and black-sesame flavours. Stars and Stripes also singles out its big, colourful 'Yumeiro' zenzai shaved ice.

F.n: Okinawa Soba Naha-tei (沖縄そば 那覇亭)
F.w: An Okinawa soba shop in central Naha picked in Mapple's Naha soba feature and profiled by Japan Travel.

F.n: C&C BREAKFAST OKINAWA (シーアンドシー ブレックファスト オキナワ)
F.w: A breakfast café a minute off Kokusai-dōri built around 'a delicious breakfast while traveling' — açaí bowls, pancakes and eggs Benedict. Ryukyu Shimpo highlighted its sweet-salty bacon-and-waffle combination.

F.n: Min'yō Stage Utahime, Kokusai-dōri (民謡ステージ歌姫)
F.w: A live Okinawan folk-song (min'yō) izakaya on Kokusai-dōri owned by Yoriko Ganeko, the singer known as 'Okinawa's songstress', with five stages a night. Food is the classic canon — gōyā champurū, rafute, fried gurukun — with Orion beer and three-year kusu awamori.

F.n: Chuko Awamori Distillery — Chuko-gura (忠孝酒造 忠孝蔵)
F.w: Founded in Tomigusuku in 1949 (as Tomigusuku Distillery); runs free ~1-hour tours of its distillery, kiln-fired pottery workshop and kusu cellars ending with a tasting of about ten awamori. Ten minutes' drive from Naha Airport.

F.n: Itoman Gyomin Shokudō (糸満漁民食堂)
F.w: Fish restaurant in the fishing town of Itoman, opened in 2013 in a building of stacked Ryūkyū limestone that won a Good Design Award and JCD Design Award. Its signature is the day's local fish butter-grilled until crisp outside and tender within.

F.n: Seifuku Shuzō awamori distillery, Ishigaki (請福酒造)
F.w: Ishigaki awamori maker founded in 1949, with a direct shop where the whole Seifuku range can be tasted and free ~15-minute factory tours at set times, no booking needed.

F.n: Yaesen Shuzō awamori distillery, Ishigaki (八重泉酒造)
F.w: Founded in 1955; the factory shop shows a 15-minute film of the distilling process and runs a tasting counter with shop-only bottles. Three Yaesen awamori won awards at a UK spirits competition (Ryukyu Shimpo).

F.n: Takamine Shuzōsho awamori distillery, Kabira (高嶺酒造所)
F.w: Small distillery beside Kabira Park making 'Omoto' awamori by hand — one of the few still using direct-fire (jika-bi) distillation; the process is visible through glass and tastings are offered.

F.n: Yakiniku Takesan-tei, Ishigaki (焼肉 たけさん亭)
F.w: Ishigaki-beef yakiniku whose owner holds cattle-auction buying rights and buys whole A4–A5 animals, so rarer cuts appear on the menu. Dinner only (closed Tue).

F.n: Yakiniku Kingyū, Ishigaki (焼肉 金牛)
F.w: Run by an Ishigaki family that has raised wagyu on the island for over 120 years; serves only its own Ishigaki beef, raised ~30 months and aged. Dinner only (closed Thu).

F.n: Taragawa awamori distillery, Miyako (多良川)
F.w: Maker of the long-selling 'Taragawa' awamori, brewed with spring water; free 40-minute tours of the plant and its cave storehouse run three times a day (closed Sun).

F.n: Yukishio Museum, Miyako (雪塩ミュージアム)
F.w: Showroom of the 'Yukishio' salt works, which makes powder-fine salt from limestone-filtered underground seawater; free guided looks at the production line, and the shop's Yukishio soft-serve is the draw.

F.n: Maeda Shokudō, Ōgimi (前田食堂)
F.w: Yanbaru noodle shop founded in 1972, on the way to Hiji Falls and Mt Yonaha; its signature gyūniku soba piles pepper-fried beef and bean sprouts on thin noodles, and weekend queues are the norm. Closes when the broth runs out.

F.n: Shima-buta Shichirin-yaki Manmi, Nago (島豚七輪焼 満味)
F.w: Reservation-essential grill house for Yanbaru island pork descended from agu: cuts and offal grilled over individual charcoal shichirin, with rare pork tongue and a horumon fried rice to finish. Dinner only (closed Sun–Mon).

F.n: Okinawa Ryōri Maruoki Shōten, Nago (沖縄料理 丸沖商店)
F.w: Nago restaurant certified under Okinawa Prefecture's 'shop where you can taste Ryūkyū cuisine' scheme; known for its agu-pork shabu-shabu course.

F.n: Kumejima no Kumesen distillery, Kume Island (久米島の久米仙)
F.w: Kume Island's best-known awamori house: a video tour of the process and free tastings from light everyday awamori to rich aged kusu, including the island-only 'Kumishima' 3-year kusu (closed Sun & holidays).

F.n: KOURI SHRIMP, Kouri Island (古宇利島 KOURI SHRIMP)
F.w: Kouri Island's garlic-shrimp stand serving Hawaiian-style shrimp plates; Stars and Stripes notes it has opened a new shop on the island.

F.n: Pork Tamago Onigiri Honten, Makishi (ポークたまごおにぎり本店)
F.w: The flagship of the 'Pōtama' shop that turned Okinawa's pork-and-egg onigiri into a takeaway icon; each one is pressed to order so the rice is hot and the egg fluffy. Opens early (7:00) for breakfast, closed Wednesdays.

F.n: Fujiya Tomari Honten (富士家 泊本店)
F.w: The name many Okinawans give first for zenzai: fluffy shaved ice frozen from the bean-cooking syrup so it never dilutes, heaped over sweet kintoki beans. Open daily, later hours in summer.

F.n: Tomari Iyumachi Fish Market (泊いゆまち)
F.w: The Okinawa fisheries co-op's market by Tomari Port, where about 70 percent of the catch sold is tuna, delivered unfrozen the day it is landed. Stalls sell sashimi, seafood bowls, shellfish and mozuku to eat on the upstairs terrace.

F.n: Kokusai-dōri Yatai-mura (国際通り屋台村)
F.w: A food-stall village opened in 2015 just off Kokusai-dōri, with more than 20 counter stalls cooking Okinawan and island dishes from local ingredients — gurukun and parrotfish sushi, Agu pork dumplings, Ishigaki beef — from 11:00. A central stage hosts island songs and dances.

F.n: Arakaki Kashiten, Shuri Samukawa (新垣菓子店 首里寒川店)
F.w: A confectioner founded in 1932 by descendants of a cook to the Ryūkyū royal court, making chinsukō and other traditional Ryūkyū sweets at its Shuri shop.

F.n: Ryūkyū Ryōri Nuchigafū (琉球料理 ぬちがふぅ)
F.ad: Tsuboya, Naha, Okinawa (hilltop off the southern end of Tsuboya Yachimun-dōri)
F.w: An elegant hilltop restaurant above the southern end of Tsuboya pottery street that Lonely Planet singles out for a memorable dinner of Ryūkyū cuisine. It is on Okinawa Prefecture's certified list of restaurants serving authentic Ryūkyū cuisine.

F.n: Kamimura Distillery Kūsu-gura (神村酒造 古酒蔵)
F.w: Awamori distillery founded in 1882 (originally in Naha's Shikina/Hantagawa), maker of Danryū — the 1968 cask-aged awamori credited with reviving post-war demand — and Shurei. Free ~40-minute tours (20 min distillery, 20 min tasting) by reservation, plus a direct shop and kūsu storage service.

F.n: Mihama Shokudō, Chatan (みはま食堂)
F.w: Local shokudō by Chatan's Mihama known for hone-jiru — pork backbones and tofu simmered in a kombu broth and eaten by hand — and hone-soba heaped with bone-in sōki; both often sell out early.

F.n: Sanchōme no Shima Soba-ya, Ginowan (3丁目の島そば屋)
F.ad: 3-10-1 Kakazu, Ginowan, Okinawa, Japan (White Papillon Sato 101)
F.w: Newer Ginowan soba shop picked among the eight best soba shops of central Okinawa in Okinawa Times' 2023 poll of 900 noodle lovers; Okinawa TV's Okitive praised its noodles, soup and toppings, notably the uneven mix of three noodle cuts.

F.n: Tacos-ya Chatan (タコス屋 北谷店)
F.ad: 1-5 Miyagi, Chatan, Okinawa, Japan (near the Sunabe Seawall)
F.w: Small taco shop on a backstreet near the Sunabe Seawall that has fed locals and visitors for about 35 years; it still fries its house-made shells to order for a chewy-crisp texture, and its Tacos-ya Plate piles tacos, taco rice, onion rings and fries on one plate.

F.n: Emi no Mise, Ōgimi (笑味の店)
F.w: Opened in 1990 by Kinjō Shōko to pass on the food culture of Ōgimi, the 'longevity village'; a farm restaurant whose reservation-only chōju-zen longevity set is built on seasonal island vegetables she grows herself. Her book of Yanbaru grandmothers' kitchen wisdom was published in 2023 (Ryukyu Shimpo).

F.n: Okashi Goten Onna (御菓子御殿 恩納店)
F.ad: Onna-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan (coastal Route 58; red-gated palace-style shop)
F.w: The red-gated seaside flagship of the confectioner behind the 'original' beni-imo tart, made from 100% Okinawan purple sweet potato from contracted farmers with no preservatives or colouring; the baking line is visible through glass and a reservation-only tart-making class runs here.

F.n: Mozuku Soba Kunnatu, Nanjō (もずくそばの店 くんなとぅ)
F.w: Facing Ōjima, a mozuku-farming centre, this shop kneads JAS-organic mozuku into its own soba noodles and serves them in a light bonito broth with tempura fried to order.

F.n: Seaside Drive-In, Onna (シーサイドドライブイン)
F.ad: Nakadomari, Onna-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan (Route 58, seaside)
F.w: Opened in 1967 under US administration and kept in its original style, neon signs and all; the signature creamy pork-bone soup is a take-out ritual for west-coast beach days, and a 24-hour take-out counter sells burgers, shaved ice and sides.

F.n: Yamakawa Shuzō awamori distillery, Motobu (山川酒造)
F.w: Motobu distillery founded in 1946 that makes awamori and long-aged kusu with Motobu spring water; cellar tours show rows of 50-year-old kusu jars and end with tastings that include 20-year-old kusu. Ryukyu Shimpo has reviewed its jar-aged 2011 vintage.

F.n: Kin Shōnyūdō cave awamori cellar — Ryū no Kura, Kin (金武鍾乳洞 古酒蔵 龍の蔵)
F.w: Since 1988 Kin Shuzō has aged its 'Ryū' awamori in a 270 m limestone cave held at a constant 18°C — billed as Japan's first cave kusu cellar — where over 14,000 bottles sit, many of them visitors' bottle-keeps for 5, 12 or 20 years; guided cave tours run three times a day.

F.n: Hateruma Shuzōsho — Awanami distillery, Hateruma Island (波照間酒造所)
F.ad: Hateruma Island, Taketomi, Yaeyama, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: The only distillery on Hateruma, Japan's southernmost inhabited island, making Awanami — the so-called 'phantom awamori' that sells out within minutes; bottles and Awanami goods are sold at the distillery shop.

F.n: Sakimoto Shuzōsho — hanazake distillery, Yonaguni (崎元酒造所)
F.w: Yonaguni's oldest distillery, still firing a traditional direct-fire pot still by hand; maker of the awamori 'Yonaguni' and of hanazake, the 60% first-run spirit that only Yonaguni is permitted to make. Distillery shop sells brewery-only bottles.

F.n: Pengin Shokudō, Ishigaki (辺銀食堂)
F.ad: Ishigaki city centre (7 min walk from Ishigaki bus terminal), Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Birthplace of Ishigaki-jima rāyu, the hand-made island-salt-and-chilli oil that started Japan's 'edible rāyu' boom; at lunch the house order is jājan-suba (thick noodles with spicy miso), served until sold out.

F.n: Akashi Shokudō, Ishigaki (明石食堂)
F.ad: 360 Ihara, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan (Akashi area, north Ishigaki)
F.w: Old-guard north-Ishigaki shokudō about 40 minutes' drive from town, with queues before opening for its soft-bone sōki Yaeyama soba — clean pork-bone broth over round straight noodles. Ranked No.1 in a 2019 Okinawa-soba ranking reported by Ryukyu Shimpo.

F.n: Arakaki Shokudō, Ishigaki — CLOSED (新垣食堂)
F.w: Ihara shokudō whose beef-broth soba, made with beef from the family's own ranch, won the original-soup division of the first Yaeyama Soba Championship. CLOSED: it shut on 27 November after 35 years (Yaeyama Mainichi).

F.n: Kuninaka Shokudō, Miyako (くになか食堂)
F.w: Locals' Miyako-soba shokudō in Miyakojima city, picked in Rurubu's eight best Miyako soba and in Mapple's Miyako dining list.

F.n: Tokuyama Shuzō awamori distillery, Irabu Island (渡久山酒造)
F.w: Compact Irabu Island awamori distillery run by the third-generation Tokuyama couple, still distilling by traditional methods; shop open 10:00-16:00 weekdays. One of three Miyako distilleries showcased at the first Shima-zake Festa (2018).

F.n: Sakana-dokoro Shiken-bara, Miyako (肴処 志堅原)
F.w: Constantly-full izakaya on Hirara's Nishizato-dōri izakaya strip, serving fresh fish from the waters around Miyako as sashimi and salt-simmered mās-ni, with island awamori.

F.n: Kumejima Soba-dokoro Yan-kō, Kume Island (久米島そば処 やん小～)
F.w: Soba shop in an old Ryūkyū-style house making hand-cut noodles with Kume's deep-sea water; the signature is a rare miso-flavoured soba piled with island-grown bean sprouts. Lunch only (11:30-13:30), closed Sundays.

F.n: Yonejima Shuzō awamori distillery, Kume Island (米島酒造)
F.w: Small Kume Island distillery founded by Tabata Ryōtoku, who was drawn by the island's abundant water and varied geology; shop open 10-12 and 14-17, closed Sundays.

F.n: Fruit Parlour Kōrakuen, Ishigaki (光楽園)
F.w: Fruit parlour popular with both locals and visitors on Ishigaki, with a long line-up of chilled sweets built on tropical island fruit; featured in its own Rurubu piece and in Mapple's Ishigaki sweets round-up.

F.n: How Tree Gelato, Ishigaki (ハウトゥリージェラート)
F.w: Specialist in cold-plate marble ice cream mixing fresh fruit from the owners' own farm with Ishigaki Island milk; seasonal (Feb-Nov).

F.n: Blue Turtle, Irabu Island (ブルー タートル)
F.ad: Irabu, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan (facing Toguchi-no-hama beach)
F.w: White sea-view café-restaurant on Irabu Island right in front of Toguchi-no-hama, one of Irabu's finest beaches; known for hamburg steak and for ice cream served over hidden layers of coloured shaved ice.

F.n: Shinzato Distillery (新里酒造)
F.ad: 12-17 Suzaki, Uruma, Okinawa 904-2234, Japan (head office 3-22-8 Koja, Okinawa City)
F.w: Founded in 1846, Shinzato is one of the oldest operating awamori distilleries in Okinawa, now run by the seventh-generation owner. It offers a roughly 45-minute factory tour combining traditional craft and modern technology, and has won the awamori grand prize at the All Japan sake competition.

F.n: Gordie's, Sunabe (ゴーディーズ)
F.w: Stand By Me-themed burger joint in a converted former on-base house near the Sunabe Seawall, serving coarse-ground, filler-free charcoal-grilled patties since 2007. Its Special Burger stacks two patties, thick bacon, a fried egg and cheese.

F.n: Pizza House Honten, Urasoe (ピザハウス 本店)
F.w: Founded in 1958 (its founders served Okinawa's first pizza), this American-style restaurant near Minatogawa Stateside Town is known for its roast beef and steaks. The main branch reopened in a 1950s-diner-style renovation on 15 March 2026 with the stated aim of becoming a '100-year restaurant'.

F.n: Miyanchi STUDIO & COFFEE, Okinawa City (みやんち STUDIO&COFFEE)
F.w: Red-tiled café and studio opened in 2012 in the hills of Okinawa City, produced by THE BOOM singer Kazufumi Miyazawa to share Okinawan folk music and food. Its signature is kara-soba, a soup-less Okinawa soba Miyazawa devised after eating a version on Ishigaki.

F.n: Tsurukame-dō Zenzai, Yomitan (鶴亀堂ぜんざい)
F.w: Zenzai shop near Zakimi Castle serving Okinawa-style zenzai — kintoki beans simmered for six hours under fluffy shaved ice. Its signature uses Yomitan's own beni-imo purple sweet potato, which dyes the ice violet under a brown-sugar syrup.

F.n: Hanaori Soba, Yomitan (花織そば)
F.w: Yomitan's flagship Okinawa-soba house on Prefectural Road 6, founded in 1988 by a former French-cuisine chef. The signature bowl tops medium-thin wavy noodles in pork-bone broth with soft-bone sōki and long-simmered pork belly; tebichi and liver-and-nira soba are also on the menu. It reopened after a renovation in 2026.

F.n: Ploughman's Lunch Bakery, Kitanakagusuku (PLOUGHMANS LUNCH BAKERY)
F.w: Bakery café in a renovated former foreign-residents' house on a jungly hilltop in Kitanakagusuku, opened in 2006 by a former Tokyo architectural designer. Its namesake one-plate Ploughman's Lunch — a British farmer's lunch of fresh vegetables with bread baked in-house — and its sandwich plates are the draw.

F.n: Shokuji-dokoro Nishikiya, Kouri Island (食事処 錦屋)
F.w: An Okinawan-cuisine and seafood-bowl canteen a short climb up from the Kouri Bridge landfall (look for the big shīsā), open 9:00–21:00; Okinawa Traveler profiles it and Mapple's Kouri Island drive guide lists it among the island's lunch stops.

F.n: Sawanoya Motobu Honten (さわのや 本部本店)
F.ad: Motobu-chō (Motobu Soba Kaidō, Prefectural Route 84), Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: One of the anchors of the 'Motobu Soba Kaidō' noodle road: noodles are hand-made the old way with wood-ash lye, giving firm, flat thick noodles with a distinctive flavour (Mapple); Stars and Stripes Okinawa features it in its guide to slurping noodles like a local.

F.n: Umi to Mugi to, Motobu (海と麦と)
F.w: Opened in Motobu in 2021 by a former French-cuisine chef whose bonito dashi has kept a queue outside ever since (OTV okitive); rurubu includes it in its 16 best Okinawa soba shops, traditional and new.

F.n: Yae Shokudō, Nago (八重食堂)
F.w: A 40-plus-year-old Nago soba shop known for topping up bowls with broth from a kettle (OCVB); voted into Okinawa Times' 2023 poll of 900 noodle fans for the best soba in the north.

F.n: Parlor Senri, Kin (パーラー千里) — CLOSED
F.w: The Kin parlor near the US base where founder Gibo Matsuzō created taco rice after opening in 1984; it closed on 29 June 2015 after 31 years (Ryukyu Shimpo). Its sister shop King Tacos, opened nearby, carries on the original recipe (rurubu).

F.n: Sakihama Seimen, Onna (崎濱製麺)
F.w: Reopened in Yamada in April 2024 as the rebrand of a Tomari (Naha) soba shop that ran 8 years; noodles are rested 3+ days and ordered kufa (hard), regular or yafa (soft), in a clear pork-bonito-kelp shio broth with no pork bones (OTV okitive). OCVB's soba-lovers' picks feature it.

F.n: Okinawa Daiichi Hotel breakfast (沖縄第一ホテル 薬膳朝食)
F.w: A five-room hotel founded in 1955 whose medicinal-herb breakfast, devised by founder Shimabukuro Yoshiko from her mother's recipes about 40 years ago, uses some 50 ingredients across 20+ Okinawan dishes (about ¥3,300). One of Naha's famous breakfasts; reservation advised.

F.n: Adachiya, Makishi (足立屋)
F.ad: Market arcade beside the former Makishi Public Market, Makishi, Naha, Okinawa
F.w: Morning-opening standing kushikatsu bar in the covered arcade by the old public market — Naha's best-known senbero (three drinks and a dish for about ¥1,000), with motsu-nikomi, kushikatsu and squid rings; busy with locals and visitors alike.

F.n: Ryūkyū Shinmen Tondō, Oroku Honten (琉球新麺 通堂 小禄本店)
F.w: The flagship of Okinawa's best-known ramen brand, billed as the world's first 'ramen with a gender': a thick, smooth tonkotsu 'men's taste' and a clear salt-chicken 'women's taste'. Open straight through from 11:00 to late night and packed with locals and visitors. The brand was also selected as a guest shop at the Shin-Yokohama Rāmen Museum.

F.n: BACAR OKINAWA, Kumoji (バカール オキナワ)
F.w: Neapolitan pizzeria by Nakamura Daisuke, trained at Tokyo's SAVOY/Seirinkan: wood-fired pies with charred, chewy and crisp textures in one slice, plus starters built on Okinawan produce. Dinner only, closed Tue–Wed.

F.n: Ōshiro Tempura, Ōjima (大城てんぷら店)
F.w: One of the three tempura stands on 'tempura island' Ōjima, under shade trees right by the water; fish, vegetable and squid tempura are fried after you order, for a few coins apiece.

F.n: Ōjima Imaiyu Market, Nanjō (奥武島いまいゆ市場)
F.ad: Entrance of Ōjima island, Tamagusuku Ōjima, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: 'Imaiyu' means 'fresh fish' in Okinawan: a small market at the island entrance selling local catches as sashimi, sushi and seafood bowls, plus produce; an on-site eating space was added so the fish can be eaten looking out over the harbour.

F.n: Jef Yonabaru (ジェフ与那原店)
F.ad: Yonabaru, Yonabaru-chō, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Head store of Jef, the Okinawa-only burger chain begun in Yonabaru in 1973 (independent since 1986); its signature Nūyaru Burger tucks an egg-bound gōyā patty into the bun, and the shop hands them to local children on Gōyā Day.

F.n: Utopia Farm Miyakojima (ユートピアファーム宮古島)
F.w: Tropical-fruit farm growing mango, pineapple and dragon fruit, with a parlour serving its own harvest as parfaits, soft serve and roll cake; the whole-Miyako-mango parfait is the order in season.

F.n: Hateruma Seitō black-sugar factory, Hateruma Island (波照間製糖)
F.ad: Hateruma Island, Taketomi-chō, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: The island's sugar mill, heart of Hateruma's main industry: about 90% of the cane is still cut by hand and boiled into kokutō within 24 hours of harvest. A working factory (crushing season roughly winter–spring) rather than a café — buy the kokutō on the island.

F.n: Ryūkyū no Shuki to Awamori Oninoude, Tsuboya (琉球ノ酒器ト泡盛 オニノウデ)
F.w: Awamori bar opened in July 2016 by sake-vessel collector Sakukawa Nagamasa, about 10 minutes' walk from Kokusai-dōri toward the Nōren market; some 400 awamori, many from the outer islands, poured from Okinawan karakara/chibugwā flasks and works by noted potters. Named for the long 'ogre's arm' bottle of old Ryūkyū; picked in BRUTUS's Naha bar issue.

F.n: Kinjō Bakery, Shuri (金城ベーカリー)
F.w: Neighbourhood bakery founded in 1952 by Kinjō Mutsuhide, a minute from Gibo monorail station, still baking about 50 kinds of nostalgic breads; added an 'omiso melon pan' using miso from Shuri's royal-era Tamanahauso. Eat-in space runs a one-hour bread buffet.

F.n: Sakaemachi Bottleneck (栄町ボトルネック)
F.w: Shōwa-mood sakaba in a former house down an alley at the west entrance of Sakaemachi Market, credited as one of the core shops of the 'second Sakaemachi boom' that drew a younger crowd to the post-war market; awamori, Okinawan snacks and a soba to finish.

F.n: Okinawan Restaurant Jimanya, Naha (じまんや 那覇店)
F.w: Okinawan restaurant in a renovated 50-year-old Okinawan house about five minutes from Miebashi station, cooking with Okinawa-raised pineapple pork and island vegetables; signature thick pork-loin tonteki, and an awamori master picks a label to suit you. English menu.

F.n: Daitō Soba Kokusai-dōri (大東そば 国際通り店)
F.w: Near Midorigaoka Park off Kokusai-dōri, the one place in Naha serving the Minami-Daitō Island soul food: thick curly noodles meant to evoke the island's rough seas, in a light pork broth, with Daitō-zushi. The owner spent a year recreating the original shop's recipe after it closed in 2022 and kept its logo.

F.n: Mutsumibashi Kadoya (むつみ橋かどや) — CLOSED
F.ad: Mutsumibashi, off Kokusai-dōri, Makishi, Naha, Okinawa
F.w: Okinawa soba specialist founded in 1952 by Ishikawa Yasushiro near Kokusai-dōri, which began selling a single kamaboko-and-ginger soba for 10 cents, once ran 24 hours and took students' watches as IOUs; known for its cloudy pork-bone broth. Closed on 20 June 2024 after 72 years.

F.n: BAR Owl, Kumoji (バー オウル)
F.ad: Kanetomo Sangyō Bldg 2F, 1-8-7 Kumoji, Naha, Okinawa 〒900-0015
F.w: Cocktail bar in Naha's Kumoji business district behind a heavy door, with a counter lined with tropical fruit; known for showy seasonal-fruit cocktails such as Okinawan mikan, and awamori cocktails. Selected for Tabelog's Bar 100 (2022).

F.n: Yappari Steak 1st, Cocktail Plaza (やっぱりステーキ 1st カクテルプラザ店)
F.w: The founding store of the Okinawa-born steak chain: it opened in Matsuyama in February 2015 as a six-seat counter selling a ¥1,000 steak, drew queues by word of mouth and grew into a nationwide chain of some 90 shops within eight years (profiled on TV Tokyo's Cambria Palace). Continues Okinawa's post-war steak-dinner culture.

F.n: Señor Taco, Plaza House (セニョール ターコ)
F.ad: Plaza House 1F, 3-1-6 Kubota, Okinawa City, Okinawa 904-0023, Japan
F.w: Opened in 1984 inside Plaza House, Señor Taco is a pioneer of Okinawa's taco scene whose shells are fried crisp outside and chewy inside; it has been loved for more than 30 years and also serves Mexican dishes like enchiladas and onion rings.

F.n: Cafe Ocean, Gate 2 Street (カフェ オーシャン)
F.w: Founded in 1967, Ocean is the oldest taco shop on Koza's Gate 2 Street in front of Kadena Air Base, frying hand-made tortillas to order with a home-style sauce taught by Americans. A taco-and-music café-bar from the post-war 'A-sign' era.

F.n: Suba-dokoro Wachichi, Okinawa City (すば処 うゎちち)
F.w: An Okinawa-soba specialist in Hiyagon whose seared soft-bone soba was certified as an Okinawa City 'Koza Choice' brand; the clear pork-and-bonito broth comes with a choice of noodles from two well-known local noodle makers. It placed 12th in OTV Okitive's reader soba ranking TOP30.

F.n: Daruma Soba, Okinawa City (だるまそば)
F.w: A hearty, queue-drawing soba shop with a pork-bone and bonito broth, chewy noodles and an unusually long menu; listed 4th in KozaWeb's Okinawa City soba ranking and 19th in OTV Okitive's reader soba TOP30.

F.n: Banjutei, Yomitan (番所亭)
F.w: A long-loved Yomitan soba house named after the old Kina banjo (district office), known for its house-made noodles, including turmeric-kneaded soba and yomogi or purple-sweet-potato variations.

F.n: Player's Cafe, Koza (プレイヤーズカフェ)
F.ad: 2-6-47 Chūō (Park Avenue), Okinawa City, Okinawa 904-0004, Japan
F.w: Opened in 1999 on Koza's Park Avenue, this café hosts live music of all genres and doubles as the lounge of Tripshot Hotels Koza; its menu draws on the owner's memories of 1970s Koza home cooking shaped by US-military canned goods. Ryukyu Shimpo reported its lunch sets as a hit with a wide range of customers.

F.n: Parlor Minato, Chatan (パーラーみなと)
F.w: Opened in 2025 in the owner's hand-converted garage, this open-air parlor serves Okinawa soba from ¥500, its broth bones boiled in seawater for depth; Okinawa Times named it among its 2025 'hidden-gem' soba eleven.

F.n: Cafe Hakoniwa, Motobu (Cafe ハコニワ)
F.ad: 2566 Izumi, Motobu-chō, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: A 50-plus-year-old house in the Izumi hills, turned into a café with antique furniture. The signature is the Hakoniwa plate, home-style rice and side dishes made with locally grown vegetables. There are also cakes and shīkwāsā juice. Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays.

F.n: Cafe Kokuu, Nakijin (カフェこくう)
F.ad: 2031-138 Moroshi, Nakijin-son, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: A hilltop café in Nakijin whose cooking draws on Japanese and macrobiotic food. The signature Kokuu plate serves more than ten kinds of organically grown island vegetables, each cooked a different way, on yachimun pottery. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

F.n: Iejima Distillery, Ie Island (伊江島蒸留所)
F.ad: 1627-3 Higashi-Ebusaki, Ie-son, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: The island's rum distillery, set up in a former bioethanol demonstration plant, makes Ie Rum Santa Maria as agricole rum from local sugarcane juice. It won Best Japanese Rum of the Year at the first Tokyo Whiskey & Spirits Competition in 2019. A distillery-limited bottling took a top gold medal in the 2026 edition. The island is a 30-minute ferry ride from Motobu Port.

F.n: Tōfu no Higa, Ishigaki (とうふの比嘉)
F.w: A family tofu maker of more than 70 years, now run by the third generation, that opens at 6:30 am and sells out before noon. It is known for yushi-dōfu, tofu ladled out before it sets. The Kariyushi set adds egg, rice or porridge, okara and soy milk. Closed Sundays.

F.n: Okinawa Soba Marukami, Miyako (沖縄そば まるかみ)
F.ad: 91 Kurima (下地来間), Shimoji, Kurima Island, Miyakojima-shi, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: A soba shop in the Kurima settlement on Kurima Island, run by a former hotel-restaurant cook. The house Marukami soba comes with homemade fresh noodles and bonito broth, topped with seasoned pork belly, tender cartilage sōki and a thin egg crepe. A plain su-soba is also on the menu. Lunch only, 11:00–14:30.

F.n: Zhyvago Coffee Works Okinawa, Chatan (ジバゴコーヒーワークス)
F.ad: Distortion Seaside Bldg, 9-46 Mihama, Chatan-chō, Nakagami District, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: A West Coast-style coffee stand on the Mihama seafront, opened in 2015, that makes each cup to order. The Ryukyu Shimpo profiled Kotaro Mikami, the Chatan Zhyvago shop manager, as the Japan AeroPress Championship winner. The brand also co-developed a coffee with JTA airline to go with chinsukō.

F.n: Jikasei-men Okinawa Soba Miyoya, Kadena (自家製麺 沖縄そば みよ家)
F.w: An Okinawa-soba specialist in Kadena making its own noodles and an additive-free broth from Rausu kombu and Makurazaki bonito; its curry soba is a signature. OTV Okitive ranked it No. 3 in its 2025 island-wide 'must-eat' Okinawa soba 15.

F.n: TESIO, Koza Gate Street (テシオ)
F.w: A ham-and-sausage maker on Koza's Gate Street, opened April 2017 by an Okinawan trained in German charcuterie methods; its products have won gold medals at IFFA, the German international meat-processing competition. Sausages are made by hand daily and a weekend hot-dog counter serves them in-shop.

F.n: Yaezen, Motobu (八重善)
F.w: A soba stop on Motobu's Route 84 'soba road', named by the OCVB soba-road itinerary for its signature bowl that combines Okinawa soba with squid-ink broth made with fresh local white squid. rurubu lists the ikasumi soba as limited to 10 servings a day, plus sōki soba and the seasonal 'Yaezen gozen' set.

F.n: Nakijin Soba (今帰仁そば)
F.w: An Okinawa soba shop in an old Ryūkyū house in a fukugi-lined village near Churaumi, known for its light but rich broth and melting nankotsu sōki. When it faced closure, fans of the shop took it over; it reopened renewed in its 10th year with outdoor seating (Okinawa Times), and ran a limited Naha pop-up in 2026.

F.n: Famille tacos, Nago (Famille)
F.w: A takeout taco stand opened in July 2025 on the national road to Junglia by a couple who cooked in French hotel restaurants; the meat takes three days to develop its flavour. Covered by Okinawa Times and Ryukyu Shimpo, and ranked No. 2 in the north in OTV Okitive's 2026 Golden Week 30, which says its 200 tacos a day sell out.

F.n: Ryūkyū Ryōri Nago-magari Restaurant, Nago (名護曲レストラン)
F.w: A long-running Ryukyu-cuisine restaurant on the coast road at Yofuke in Nago, listed by rurubu, Okinawa Traveler and the OCVB; rurubu notes the owner builds menus from rare and nutritious seasonal ingredients. The wide menu runs from Okinawan set meals and soba to Western dishes like taco rice and steak.

F.n: CAFE FUKURUBI, Kouri Island (カフェ フクルビ)
F.w: A café-restaurant on high ground near Heart Rock on Kouri Island's north side, with a 180-degree panorama of the horizon from its terrace. It cooks with prefectural ingredients and especially Kouri Island's own pure brown sugar, used in its signature black-sugar French toast.

F.n: Kōhī Sakan Inshallah, Kokusai-dōri (珈琲茶館インシャラー)
F.w: Coffee house on Kokusai-dōri trading since 1974, themed on Arabia as coffee's birthplace and serving Turkish and Arabic coffees. Its signature 'Paris no Romance' has rose cream swirling in the cup as the coffee is poured at the table.

F.n: Live House Shimauta, Kokusai-dōri (ライブハウス島唄)
F.ad: Haisai Okinawa Bldg 3F, 1-2-31 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa
F.w: Home stage of Nēnēs, the women's vocal group credited with sparking the shima-uta boom; they play several nights a week (three sets a night), with other local acts on the rest. Okinawan food and drink served, no time limit on the live charge.

F.n: Okinawa Soba Kintarō, Nanjō (沖縄そば 金太郎)
F.w: A local soba shop in Tamagusuku-Funakoshi known for a rich pork-bone soup and huge 'Jirō-inspired' bowls heaped with vegetables, with a three-meat Okinawa soba as its standard. Its owner chairs the Nanjō Okinawa-soba stamp rally promoting the city as a soba town.

F.n: Yukui-dokoro Washima, Kume Island (ゆくい処 笑島)
F.w: Kume-jima's kuruma-prawn soba, built on an Okinawa-soba dashi with a paste of the island's farmed kuruma prawns and local miso, won the grand prix at the 'Nippon no Takaramono' world competition held in Singapore. The shop sells around 60 bowls a day and often sells out.

F.n: Wayama Mozuku, Zamami (和山海雲)
F.w: A mozuku farmer's own restaurant three minutes' walk from Zamami port, serving soba made with thick mozuku grown in the Kerama sea; Okinawa Times praised the firm noodles' match with the seaweed's texture. It also sells its mozuku and runs snorkel tours.

F.n: Boku no Mise Ojisan, Zamami (ぼくの店 おじさん)
F.w: A local favourite three minutes' walk from Zamami port, known for a hearty katsudon alongside soba and chanpurū lunch plates. It is listed on Zamami Village's official guide map.

F.n: Minatomachi Parlor, Itoman (港町パーラー)
F.ad: 989-83 Itoman, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan (Itoman Market Itomāru)
F.w: A small counter opened in April 2025 inside Itoman's public market 'Itomāru' by the second-generation head of Kinshiro Sengyo, a fish shop trading in Itoman for 35+ years; the owner fillets the day's catch on the spot for generous local-fish bowls. Ryukyu Shimpo's 'Uchinā Ajimāi' series and OTV Okitive both featured it.

F.n: Kikunotsuyu Shuzō awamori distillery, Miyako (菊之露酒造)
F.w: Founded in 1928 in Hirara, Kikunotsuyu is one of Miyako's oldest and best-known awamori distillers, using the island's mineral-rich hard water from its coral-limestone bedrock; its aged awamori features in the Okinawa Regional Taxation Bureau's awamori appraisal.

F.n: Tamanaha Shuzōsho awamori distillery, Ishigaki (玉那覇酒造所)
F.w: Billed as Yaeyama's oldest awamori distillery, the family-run Tamanaha makes Tama no Tsuyu, a rare Ishigaki brand seldom found on the mainland; its kūsu appears in the Okinawa Regional Taxation Bureau's awamori appraisal results.

F.n: Donan (Kokusen Awamori) hanazake distillery, Yonaguni (どなん 国泉泡盛)
F.w: Distilling on Yonaguni since 1958, Kokusen makes Donan, including the 60 % hanazake that only Yonaguni's distilleries are licensed to produce — awamori's highest strength, originally a ceremonial spirit. Visitors can see production and buy small bottles at the hilltop plant it moved to in 2011.

F.n: Ikemajima gelato cafe Ninufa, Ikema Island (ニヌファ)
F.w: An Italian-style gelato café on Ikema Island whose name means 'North Star' in Miyako dialect; every seat on its coral-rock terrace faces the sea. Gelato is made without artificial flavouring, colouring or preservatives in local flavours, with wood-fired pizza alongside.

F.n: Ishigaki City Public Market (石垣市公設市場)
F.w: Ishigaki's 'kitchen' since 1899 (on this site since 1904), a three-storey public market in the Euglena Mall arcade: local produce and fish at street level, the Ishigaki City specialty-products centre above and a shokudō on top; an eat-in space was added in the May 2021 renewal.

F.n: Okinohikari Shuzō awamori distillery, Miyako (沖之光酒造)
F.w: Founded in 1948 (as Kosa Shuzō; Okinohikari since 1979), this Hirara distillery keeps about 70 % of its stock as aged kūsu; its 100 % ten-year-aged Okinohikari won the Okinawa Regional Taxation Bureau Director's Award at the 2005 awamori appraisal.

F.n: Yuunami Sakashita (自家製生麺 ゆうなみ 坂下店)
F.ad: Terrace Sakashita 1F, 301-15 Matsukawa, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: A local Okinawa-soba shop whose house-made fresh noodles are blended with whole-wheat flour. You can pick thin, flat or mugwort noodles for the signature nankotsu sōki soba, and the pork-and-bonito broth is rich enough to drink to the last drop. Readers voted it into the Okinawa Times 2023 '900 noodle lovers pick' Okinawa-soba ranking (southern edition).

F.n: Soba-dokoro Kikuya, Oroku (そば処 きくや)
F.w: A red-tiled house next to the owner's home, about five minutes by car from Naha Airport. The light broth of pork bone, bonito, kombu and vegetables is simmered for two days. The menu has sanmai-niku soba, yushi-tōfu soba and black-sugar zenzai, and it closes when sold out (around 3 pm). It was picked in the Okinawa Times 2023 reader poll of Okinawa-soba shops (southern edition).

F.n: Okinawa Jiryōri Angama, Kokusai-dōri (沖縄地料理 あんがま)
F.w: An Okinawan-cuisine and folk-song restaurant just inside the south entrance of Kokusai-dōri. The entrance is built like a red-tiled, stone-walled house and is topped by a giant mask from Ishigaki's Angama Bon festival. The menu has about 60 dishes made with island vegetables, pork and local seafood, including gōyā chanpurū, tebichi and sōki-ni, plus four set courses. Min'yō singers play every night in the third-floor hall.

F.n: Shima-uta to Jiryōri Tubarama, Kokusai-dōri (島唄と地料理 とぅばらーま)
F.w: An Okinawan-cuisine restaurant on Kokusai-dōri, a one-minute walk from Makishi Station, with an interior that recreates a pre-war Okinawan townscape. Lunch is Okinawa soba and chanpurū set meals, and sanshin shima-uta (island-song) bands play every night. OTV Okitive featured it for blending tradition with modern twists such as an Okinawan-style fried rice.

F.n: Imai Pan, Maji (いまいパン 真地本店)
F.w: A neighbourhood boulangerie five minutes' walk from the Shikinaen World Heritage garden. About 80 kinds of bread fill the small shop, and owner Yōsuke Imai bakes from 5 am through the day using local ingredients such as Tamagusuku Farm milk from Nanjō and Haebaru eggs. With the Maji residents' association it also runs 'Ōchō Shokupan Shikinaen', which sells a premium 'Ryūkyū king's' loaf at the garden entrance. Okinawa Times reported on that loaf.
